regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First-line dMMR/MSI-H advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: First-line dMMR/MSI-H endometrial carcinoma, recurrent or primary advanced, unsuitable for potentially curative surgery, radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy, and eligible for systemic therapy.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line systemic treatment for selected dMMR/MSI-H recurrent or primary advanced endometrial carcinoma; confirm curative local options are unsuitable.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Durvalumab blocks the PD-L1 checkpoint, paclitaxel stabilises microtubules and carboplatin causes DNA crosslinks. The two cytotoxics end after induction; checkpoint blockade continues during maintenance.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Day 1 every 21 days: all three medicines for 4–6 cycles. If continuing, durvalumab alone starts 3 weeks after the last combination infusion, then repeats every 28 days while helping and tolerated.
key_points: Day 1 every 21 days: all three medicines for 4–6 cycles. If continuing, durvalumab alone starts 3 weeks after the last combination infusion, then repeats every 28 days while helping and tolerated.
Induction: durvalumab 1120 mg, paclitaxel 175 mg/m² and carboplatin AUC5 (GFR capped at 125 mL/min).
Maintenance: durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 28 days; at ≤30 kg, use 20 mg/kg until weight exceeds 30 kg.

NCCP 00953 v1a pp5–10 covers ICI event-specific actions, paclitaxel counts/hepatic function/neuropathy and carboplatin GFR safeguards. Check active phase and competing causes. Independent clinical approval pending.
regimen_profiles.review_status: Independent clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending

treatment_rationale.summary: The aim is to control the cancer, ease or prevent symptoms and delay worsening. Your team can explain the benefit they expect for you and your other options.
treatment_rationale.setting: First-line systemic treatment for selected dMMR/MSI-H recurrent or primary advanced endometrial carcinoma; confirm curative local options are unsuitable.
factors: First-line dMMR/MSI-H endometrial carcinoma, recurrent or primary advanced, unsuitable for potentially curative surgery, radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy, and eligible for systemic therapy. ECOG 0–1; ECOG 2 by consultant discretion. Adequate marrow, renal and hepatic function.
alternatives: Review curative local therapy eligibility first; discuss other systemic or symptom-directed care according to the individual context.
limitations: This was a prespecified exploratory subgroup. A separate study arm also used olaparib; olaparib is not part of this NCCP regimen.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: The aim is to control the cancer, ease or prevent symptoms and delay worsening. Your team can explain the benefit they expect for you and your other options.
patient_selection.disease_and_biomarker_context: First-line dMMR/MSI-H endometrial carcinoma, recurrent or primary advanced, unsuitable for potentially curative surgery, radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy, and eligible for systemic therapy.
eligibility_orientation: First-line dMMR/MSI-H endometrial carcinoma, recurrent or primary advanced, unsuitable for potentially curative surgery, radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy, and eligible for systemic therapy. ECOG 0–1; ECOG 2 by consultant discretion. Adequate marrow, renal and hepatic function.
exclusion_orientation: Pregnancy, breastfeeding, relevant drug/excipient hypersensitivity and severe hepatic impairment (paclitaxel). Review immunosuppression, transplant, autoimmunity, IBD, neuropathy and prior checkpoint exposure.
important_cautions: Systemic immunosuppression over 10 mg/day prednisolone equivalent, significant autoimmune disease, previous IBD, prior CRT pneumonitis, immunodeficiency or transplant immunosuppression.
Assess function-limiting neuropathy before paclitaxel. Reconcile previous checkpoint exposure, allergy, fertility and pregnancy considerations.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Combination high; maintenance durvalumab alone minimal.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Induction: carboplatin AUC5 is high emetogenic risk; use verified local prophylaxis and rescue plan.
Paclitaxel first dose requires taxane hypersensitivity premedication according to NCCP and local administration policy.
Maintenance: no taxane premedication; durvalumab alone has minimal emetogenic risk.
counselling: Combination treatment has high sickness risk, mainly from carboplatin. Take your prescribed prevention and rescue medicines as directed. Durvalumab alone has minimal sickness risk, so the plan may change.
The team gives medicines to lower the chance of an infusion reaction, including a steroid and antihistamine according to its plan. Tell the nurse immediately about wheeze, flushing or faintness.
Contact the team early about numb or painful hands or feet, difficulty with buttons or walking, or troublesome muscle or joint aches.
Carry your immunotherapy alert card during and after treatment. Show it to any urgent-care clinician. Do not start, stop or change steroids yourself.

Discuss pregnancy, contraception and fertility before treatment. Durvalumab requires effective contraception during treatment and for at least three months after the last dose; ask your team for the longest interval required by any medicine you receive. Do not breastfeed during treatment.

baseline: Validated dMMR/MSI-H result and clinical suitability; ECOG 0–1 (ECOG 2 only by consultant discretion).
FBC, renal and liver function, thyroid function and random glucose.
Isotope GFR preferred for carboplatin; estimate GFR/CrCl if needed. Neuropathy assessment and audiology when indicated.
before_each_cycle: FBC, kidney and liver function, thyroid tests and random glucose. Cortisol and neuropathy assessment as clinically indicated.
If carboplatin dosing uses an estimated GFR/CrCl, calculate from serum creatinine taken within 48 hours. If isotope GFR used, review if creatinine rises above 110% of value at isotope measurement.

longitudinal_schedule.note: Hepatitis B/C testing may be arranged under local policy or individual risk. This protocol does not list universal baseline viral tests or cortisol. Tell the team about steroid use when hormone tests are arranged.

priority_toxicities: Pneumonitis · lung inflammation — New cough or breathlessness needs an immediate oncology call. Severe breathing difficulty needs 112 or 999.
Infection or low blood counts — Fever, chills or sudden illness can be serious even with a normal temperature. Call oncology immediately.
Colitis · bowel inflammation — New or worsening diarrhoea, belly pain or blood in stools needs urgent oncology advice.
Hormone problems — Severe weakness, dizziness, vomiting or extreme thirst can signal changes in hormone or blood-sugar levels. Call oncology immediately.
Infusion allergy — Tell the nurse immediately if you feel flushed, wheezy, dizzy or unwell during a drip.
monitoring_and_toxicity.disease_monitoring: Imaging and other tests follow the consultant’s treatment plan.

test_specific_details.label: Full blood count, renal and liver function
test_specific_details.purpose: Assess marrow and organ function and inform component-specific eligibility and modification.
test_specific_details.timing: Baseline and regularly thereafter; estimated GFR for carboplatin uses a creatinine within 48 hours.

test_specific_details.label: Thyroid function and random glucose
test_specific_details.purpose: Detect thyroid dysfunction and hyperglycaemia during immune therapy.

test_specific_details.label: Cortisol
test_specific_details.purpose: Investigate suspected adrenal or pituitary dysfunction; review steroid timing and urgency.
test_specific_details.timing: As clinically indicated. Routine baseline cortisol and universal HBV/HCV testing are not listed under this regimen; use local policy and clinical risk for viral testing.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Day 1 every 21 days: all three medicines for 4–6 cycles. If continuing, durvalumab alone starts 3 weeks after the last combination infusion, then repeats every 28 days while helping and tolerated.
administration.route_and_duration: All medicines are given into a vein. On combination days durvalumab is given first over about 1 hour, then paclitaxel over about 3 hours and carboplatin over about 30 minutes. Allow extra time for review, premedicines, blood results and preparation. Durvalumab alone takes about an hour.
practical_workflow: Document the last combination cycle and date, then the first durvalumab-only dose and the new 28-day interval.
Record the current phase on the consent discussion record, passport, card and any dose-adjustment assessment.

evidence_at_a_glance.trial: DUO-E, phase III double-blind randomised trial
evidence_at_a_glance.population: People with newly diagnosed advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. The Irish regimen is limited to the dMMR/MSI-H group.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: Durvalumab plus carboplatin/paclitaxel followed by durvalumab alone versus chemotherapy plus placebo followed by placebo. A separate arm also included olaparib.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: The Irish 00953a indication is the dMMR/MSI-H group receiving maintenance durvalumab alone.

endpoints.result_text: HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.22–0.80), durvalumab arm versus control.
endpoints.interpretation: Prespecified exploratory subgroup, time-to-event comparison rather than absolute benefit or median individual survival.
endpoints.analysis_status: Published primary phase III report, dMMR subgroup.

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: The dMMR subgroup receiving durvalumab had a lower rate of progression or death over follow-up (hazard ratio 0.42, 95% confidence interval 0.22–0.80). This compares groups over time and does not predict how long treatment will help one person.
limitations: This was a prespecified exploratory subgroup. A separate study arm also used olaparib; olaparib is not part of this NCCP regimen.
